q: In a child with whooping cough, all are true EXCEPT:
o: Higher risk of brain damage under 1 year
Erythromycin completely resolves symptoms within 10 days
e: Antibiotics shorten infectivity but do not stop the cough.

q: In pertussis, all are true EXCEPT:
o: Young infants may have no whoop
Infectivity starts in the paroxysmal stage
e: The catarrhal stage is the most infectious.

q: The main cause of death in diphtheria is:
The most important treatment of diphtheria is:
e: Antitoxin neutralises unbound toxin; plus penicillin.

q: A 7-year-old has trismus and painful spasms after a nail wound; he is alert. The antibiotic of choice is:
e: Plus HTIG, diazepam and wound care.

q: Any child under 15 with acute flaccid paralysis should have:
o: Notification and 2 stool samples 24 h apart within 14 days
